main.title: Crysis
main.subtitle: The Jungle Is a Set of Possibilities
main.summary: Crytek combines a tropical battlefield with the Nanosuit, giving players several ways to approach an outpost.

cards.heading: Crytek opens the jungle
cards.text: Crytek released Crysis for PC in North America on November 13, 2007. The shooter places its protagonist in a tropical archipelago with broad sightlines, vehicles and vegetation that support different approaches to an objective. The Nanosuit supplies armour, speed, strength and cloaking, while CryENGINE 2 makes the reactive landscape a demanding showcase for PC hardware.

cards.heading: The Nanosuit's four modes
cards.text: The Nanosuit's modes share a limited energy supply. Armour absorbs damage, Speed accelerates movement, Strength increases physical power and Cloak temporarily hides the player. Switching between them can turn an approach into a sequence: sneak closer, move an obstacle, then escape to another position. Energy consumption prevents one advantage from lasting indefinitely.

cards.heading: Choosing an approach
cards.text: An outpost can be watched from a hill, approached through the water, entered under cloak or attacked from a vehicle. Missions and geography establish the destination, while the space around it leaves room to choose a route. Buildings, vegetation and distance offer different uses for the Nanosuit's abilities.

cards.heading: Building the jungle with CryENGINE 2
cards.text: CryENGINE 2 renders dense vegetation, dynamic shadows, water and physical objects across these large spaces. DirectX 9 and DirectX 10 support lets the game run with different settings on a range of PCs, though its highest settings became a demanding benchmark. The pre-release demo also included the Sandbox 2 editor, allowing players to examine the tools behind the scenery.

cards.heading: Creating with Sandbox 2
cards.text: Sandbox 2 lets users place terrain, vegetation, objects, artificial intelligence and events directly in the three-dimensional world. Crytek supported modding with updates, portals and SDKs. Those tools extended the game beyond its campaign and gave players a way to build their own environments with the same technology.

cards.heading: A benchmark for PC hardware
cards.text: Running Crysis at high settings became an informal measure of a PC's power. Scalable options let players adjust the load, while maximum quality encouraged benchmarks, hardware comparisons and upgrades. Its reputation also depended on what that technology supported: long distances, physical objects and several routes through a battle.

main.title: Uncharted: Drake's Fortune
main.summary: Uncharted: Drake's Fortune is a 2007 action-adventure game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3.

cards.heading: Drake searches for El Dorado
cards.text: Uncharted: Drake's Fortune is a 2007 action-adventure game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3. It is the first game in the Uncharted series and follows Nathan Drake, the supposed descendant of explorer Sir Francis Drake, as he searches for the lost treasure of El Dorado with journalist Elena Fisher and mentor Victor Sullivan.

cards.heading: A new adventure for Naughty Dog
cards.text: Naughty Dog began development in 2005, choosing a third-person adventure with human characters and platforming. Films, pulp magazines and movie serials shaped the look and tone. The team repeatedly revised the story, code and design as it built the game, contributing to delays.

cards.heading: Reception and the series
cards.text: Extensively marketed as a PlayStation exclusive, Uncharted: Drake's Fortune received generally favorable reviews, with praise for its characters and voice acting, story, music, technical achievements, and production values, drawing similarities to blockbuster films. It faced some criticism for its graphical issues, short length, vehicle sections, and marked difficulty. Uncharted: Drake's Fortune sold one million copies after ten weeks of release. It was followed by the sequel Uncharted 2: Among Thieves in 2009, and was re-released on PlayStation 4 as part of Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection.

main.title: Rock Band
main.subtitle: Four different parts become one performance
main.summary: Harmonix broadened the plastic-guitar phenomenon into a shared performance for guitar, bass, drums and vocals.

cards.heading: Building the living-room band
cards.text: Rock Band first reached North American PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 players on November 20, 2007. Developed by Harmonix, published by MTV Games and distributed by Electronic Arts, it expanded the musical-controller idea beyond the guitar. Up to four people follow separate guitar, bass, drum and vocal parts within the same song. The original disc contains 58 tracks, including established rock artists and bonus songs from smaller acts. PlayStation 2 and Wii editions followed, with differences in their tour features and downloadable-content support.

cards.heading: Keeping one another on stage
cards.text: A band shares its score, but each player can choose a different difficulty. Guitarists watch note lanes, the drummer follows pads and a pedal, and the singer matches pitch against a vocal line. Overdrive adds a collective decision: its energy can raise the score or help bring a failed band member back into the song. The result is more than four independent score attacks. An experienced player can support a newcomer, and a familiar recording becomes a small exercise in listening and cooperation.

main.title: Mass Effect
main.subtitle: A Galaxy Built Through Choices
main.summary: BioWare follows Commander Shepard across a galaxy of rival species, combining conversations, exploration and squad combat.

cards.heading: Shepard enters the galaxy
cards.text: BioWare released Mass Effect for Xbox 360 in North America on November 20, 2007. Commander Shepard explores a science-fiction galaxy through conversations, planetary expeditions and real-time combat with a squad. Players choose Shepard's appearance and class, then make decisions that shape relationships and missions. The dialogue wheel, galaxy map and Codex help organise the journey.

cards.heading: Choosing through the dialogue wheel
cards.text: The dialogue wheel presents short phrases that suggest Shepard's intention. Players can prepare a reply while another character is speaking, keeping conversation moving between performances. The chosen phrase is a summary of the spoken line, so its position and wording must convey tone as well as content. Investigation options and diplomatic or forceful answers become familiar parts of the interface.

cards.heading: A customisable Alliance officer
cards.text: Players choose Shepard's sex, appearance, class and background, while the character begins with an established position as an Alliance officer. Paragon and Renegade choices offer diplomatic and harsher ways of exercising authority, affecting dialogue opportunities. Later games can import a save file, carrying parts of this version of Shepard into the next adventure.

cards.heading: Life on the Citadel
cards.text: The Citadel introduces the galaxy's institutions through its embassies, security offices and commercial districts. Walking between them brings encounters with different species and their competing interests. The Codex adds background to what Shepard sees and hears, while elevators and rapid transit connect the station's separate areas.

cards.heading: Direct combat and squad commands
cards.text: Shepard moves and fires directly, with a power wheel available to select abilities and issue commands to two companions. Class and equipment choices help the squad deal with shields, armour and other obstacles. Biotic and technological powers add options for controlling enemies or supporting an attack, bringing party management into the firefight.

cards.heading: Exploring with the Mako
cards.text: The M35 Mako carries the squad across the rough surfaces of secondary planets. Players can travel towards outposts, anomalies and mineral deposits scattered across broad landscapes. Its handling drew criticism, but the vehicle also gives these expeditions a sense of distance distinct from the main story's more enclosed locations.

cards.heading: Carrying a save into the sequel
cards.text: The trilogy allows later games to import decisions from an earlier save. People met, completed missions and positions taken can affect the following adventure. The consequences vary in scale, but the continuity lets a player recognise a personal history in the next chapter. A save carries part of Shepard's story beyond a single game.

main.title: Tekken 6
main.summary: Tekken 6 is a 2007 fighting game developed and published by Namco Bandai Games.

cards.heading: From arcades to home consoles
cards.text: Tekken 6 is a 2007 fighting game developed and published by Namco Bandai Games. It is the sixth main and seventh overall installment in the Tekken franchise. It was released on arcades in November 2007 as the first game running on the PlayStation 3-based System 357 arcade board. A year later, the game received an update, subtitled Bloodline Rebellion; both versions also saw a limited release in North America. A home version based on the update was released for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in October 2009; this was the first time a main installment was produced for a non-Sony console. A port to the PlayStation Portable was also released shortly after.

cards.heading: Rage and Scenario Campaign
cards.text: Produced by Katsuhiro Harada, Tekken 6 adds Rage, which increases a fighter's strength when health is low. The home release also includes Scenario Campaign, a beat 'em up mode following Lars Alexandersson and the robot Alisa Bosconovitch. Lars loses his memory during an attack on the Mishima Zaibatsu and sets out to recover his identity. Completing missions awards equipment that can enhance a character's abilities.

cards.heading: Reception and sales
cards.text: The game received generally positive reviews. Critics praised the visuals and the new fight mechanics but had mixed opinions about the handling of the Scenario Campaign. Nevertheless, the PSP port was also well-received for how faithful it was to the initial console versions. The game's sales have reached 5.6 million copies worldwide. It was later re-released with the spin-off Tekken Tag Tournament 2 and Soulcalibur V for the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3. A sequel, Tekken 7, was released in 2015.

main.title: Professor Layton and the Diabolical Box
main.subtitle: A mystery boards the train
main.summary: Professor Layton and the Diabolical Box is Level-5's second Nintendo DS puzzle adventure starring Hershel Layton and Luke. A box said to kill whoever opens it sends them on a railway journey through several locations. Known as Pandora's Box in Europe, the game expands the first adventure's village-sized investigation into a trip with changing destinations. Residents still offer brainteasers in exchange for attention or assistance. The journey supplies a larger mystery, while each conversation can pause it for a smaller problem to consider at leisure.

cards.heading: A mystery boards the train
cards.text: Professor Layton and the Diabolical Box is Level-5's second Nintendo DS puzzle adventure starring Hershel Layton and Luke. A box said to kill whoever opens it sends them on a railway journey through several locations. Known as Pandora's Box in Europe, the game expands the first adventure's village-sized investigation into a trip with changing destinations. Residents still offer brainteasers in exchange for attention or assistance. The journey supplies a larger mystery, while each conversation can pause it for a smaller problem to consider at leisure.

cards.heading: Reasoning in the palm of a hand
cards.text: Puzzles use the stylus to enter numbers, select an answer, mark a location or rearrange pieces. Their picarat values reward a correct solution, with the first wrong attempts reducing the points available. Hint coins found around the locations can buy assistance, allowing progress without imposing a time limit on thought. The familiar system makes a new destination immediately approachable. A scene can contain a clue, a conversation and a hidden coin, so looking around remains useful even before the next puzzle has appeared on screen.

cards.heading: Tea, photographs and a hamster
cards.text: Puzzle rewards feed three smaller activities: exercising a hamster, repairing a camera and collecting ingredients for tea. Brewing and serving a suitable cup gives the people encountered another reason to matter beyond their next riddle. The camera and hamster similarly turn progress into objects the player can revisit between chapters. These diversions give the railway mystery a relaxed domestic texture. A dangerous rumour may be driving the investigation, but Layton's travelling routine still has room for a drink, a repair and another patient attempt at a puzzle.

main.title: Wii Fit
main.summary: Wii Fit is a 2007 exergaming video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii.

cards.heading: Exercise on the Balance Board
cards.text: Wii Fit is a 2007 exergaming video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii. It features a variety of yoga, strength training, aerobics, and balance mini-games for use with the Wii Balance Board peripheral. Designer Hiroshi Matsunaga described the game as a "way to help get families exercising together". It has since been adopted by various health clubs around the world, and has previously been used for physiotherapy rehabilitation in children and in nursing homes to improve posture in the elderly.

cards.heading: Reception and worldwide sales
cards.text: Wii Fit received mixed to positive reviews, with some critics questioning the intensity of its workouts. Its Balance Board package sold 22.67 million copies, showing the reach of an exercise game built around a new peripheral.

cards.heading: Wii Fit Plus expands the activities
cards.text: Nintendo released Wii Fit Plus in October 2009, adding games and activities to the original package. It sold 21.13 million copies, bringing the combined total for the two editions to 43.8 million.

main.title: Lost Odyssey
main.subtitle: An immortal journey through the lives that do not last
main.summary: Lost Odyssey first launched for Xbox 360 in Japan on December 6, 2007, before reaching other regions in 2008. Mistwalker and feelplus built the adventure around Kaim, an immortal warrior whose missing memories return against the background of a magical industrial revolution. Hironobu Sakaguchi brought together artist Takehiko Inoue, writer Kiyoshi Shigematsu and composer Nobuo Uematsu. The contrast between a life that continues and the people it leaves behind gives this grand fantasy a quieter centre: memory is a burden as well as a way of recovering who Kaim is.

cards.heading: A thousand years of remembering
cards.text: Lost Odyssey first launched for Xbox 360 in Japan on December 6, 2007, before reaching other regions in 2008. Mistwalker and feelplus built the adventure around Kaim, an immortal warrior whose missing memories return against the background of a magical industrial revolution. Hironobu Sakaguchi brought together artist Takehiko Inoue, writer Kiyoshi Shigematsu and composer Nobuo Uematsu. The contrast between a life that continues and the people it leaves behind gives this grand fantasy a quieter centre: memory is a burden as well as a way of recovering who Kaim is.

cards.heading: What immortals learn from mortals
cards.text: Its turn-based battles make that relationship between mortal and immortal characters tangible. Mortals gain skills as they level up; immortals can learn from them through Skill Link, or master abilities carried by accessories. The front row also forms a defensive wall that reduces damage to allies behind it. With an enhancement ring equipped, timing the release of the right trigger as two circles overlap strengthens the ring’s effect on an ordinary attack. These small decisions sit inside a traditional journey through towns, fields and a world map. The original game later joined Xbox One backward compatibility and was released digitally in 2016.

main.title: PixelJunk Monsters
main.summary: PixelJunk Monsters is a tower defense video game developed by Q-Games for the PlayStation 3.

cards.text: PixelJunk Monsters is a tower defense video game developed by Q-Games for the PlayStation 3. The second game in the PixelJunk series, it was originally released in Japan on December 6, 2007 and worldwide by Sony Computer Entertainment on the PlayStation Store on January 24, 2008. The game was released for the PlayStation Portable under the title PixelJunk Monsters Deluxe.
PixelJunk Monsters Encore, an expansion pack for the game, was released on April 24, 2008 in Japan; May 8, 2008 in North America; and May 15, 2008 in Europe.
Double Eleven developed PixelJunk Monsters Ultimate HD for PlayStation Vita, Windows, Mac OS X and Linux in 2013. It later brought the original game to Wii U in 2016.
In 2018, PixelJunk Monsters 2 was released, incorporating 3D graphics and new features.

main.title: Patapon
main.subtitle: An army answers every drumbeat
main.summary: Pyramid and Japan Studio made rhythm the language of command: a small army repeats the player’s drum patterns as it marches towards Earthend.

cards.heading: A tribe follows its invisible deity
cards.text: Pyramid and Japan Studio released Patapon for PSP in Japan in December 2007, followed by North America and Europe in February 2008. The player guides a tribe of small, one-eyed warriors by playing drum patterns that order them to march, attack, defend or retreat. Their journey towards Earthend and the mysterious "IT" brings encounters with giant beasts and the rival Zigoton tribe. Designer Hiroyuki Kotani developed the concept after seeing French artist Rolito's Patapon designs; the name came from an old French children's song.

cards.heading: Keep the beat, rebuild the army
cards.text: Each PSP face button plays a different drum. Commands follow four-beat patterns, with a pulsing screen border marking the rhythm. Accurate sequences maintain a combo and build Fever, strengthening the army; losing the beat breaks the chain. During Fever, Miracles can change the weather to help the tribe cross a hot desert or extend the reach of its arrows. Between battles, players gather weapons and materials to create stronger warriors. A fallen Patapon leaves a cap that must be recovered if the warrior is to be revived.

cards.heading: The warriors sing the command back
cards.text: Kemmei Adachi served as composer while Kotani wrote the lyrics. Kemmei was recruited from the game's conception and proposed ideas to develop the game. Music was composed of multiple African instruments. Pyramid proposed to make the Patapons sing back to the player once a command was sent. Vocals for the songs were provided by Kotani's son who was 10 years old at the time.
